absent: Weight averaging, entity key computation and virtual-time comparison definitions beyond their use in accumulation and ordering.
Full fair class operations including dequeue, pick, preemption and tick integration beyond current refresh and insertion.
Lock ordering between cache group lock, CPU epoch lock, runqueue lock and RCU read sections.
Validity and capacity predicates for LLC selection and epoch and runtime update mechanics.
Complete sysctl ranges, feature flag definitions and scheduler statistics counter layouts.
Scheduler cache enablement condition and task work lifecycle beyond queuing and single-shot reset.

findings.text: Reference descriptor associates a scheduler instance and source mask with a contiguous identifier interval and a shard subrange. It carries base offset and count plus shard bounds expressed as signed indices.
Masks built through the helper record base, logical count and allocated word count derived from allocation size, with storage sized to cover allocated identifiers.

Default tunables: tunable scaling uses logarithmic mode; base slice and its normalized copy are 700000; migration cost is 500000; CFS bandwidth slice is 5000; NUMA balancing promote rate limit is 65536. Deprecated thermal decay shift option is acknowledged and ignored.

Weight multiplier constant is all-bits-set unsigned with shift 32. Cache epoch period is one hundredth of HZ representing 10 ms with affinity timeout 5 representing 50 ms. LLC defaults are aggregation tolerance 1, imbalance 20, over-aggregation 50, with epoch period and timeout tracking the macros. NUMA imbalance minimum is 2.

Fair scheduler exposes optional kernel tunables for CFS bandwidth slice and NUMA promote rate limit with read-write permissions and bounded integer handling, registered during init under the kernel table when corresponding features are enabled.
Fair scheduling class object is declared for linkage across the scheduler; its operations are defined elsewhere.

Entities sharing the same queue are recognized as one group; otherwise no group is returned. Parent lookup either follows the stored parent link or constantly yields absence depending on build variant. Idle classification either checks task policy directly or for groups consults group idleness.
Extremum helpers retain the larger or smaller virtual runtime under virtual-time ordering.

Each queue maintains accumulated weighted virtual time and total weight keyed by entity position. A feature-gated paranoid path validates multiplication and addition for overflow and on failure widens a scaling shift and rebuilds both accumulators by walking the ordered timeline from its leftmost node before retrying.
Repeated overflow escalates the scaling shift and becomes fatal once the shift reaches ten, indicating unrecoverable accumulation growth.

Eligibility threshold is derived from the queue zero point plus the signed weighted average offset plus one, excluding the current entity contribution and adjusting negative totals toward the floor. Callers are expected to supply a queued current entity; absence is flagged as unexpected.
Queue minimum slice is the lesser of the current runnable entity slice when present and the root subtree minimum when present, defaulting to maximum when neither applies.

Timeline ordering follows entity precedence. Each node caches subtree minima for virtual time and slice and subtree maxima for slice; updates recompute a node from its own values plus both children and report whether all aggregates stayed unchanged, with a copy helper transferring all three aggregates between entities.

Insertion expects the top-level fair queue and a task entity, recording unexpected cases. It folds the entity into weighted accumulators, seeds its cached minima and maxima from its own virtual time and slice, then inserts into the augmented ordered timeline.

Protection deadline starts at entity deadline bounded by base or queue-minimum slice and entity slice, optionally tightened using eligibility threshold or virtual-time-plus-slice conversion under feature gates; later updates only move it earlier using queue minimum and averaged virtual time, and cancellation collapses it back to current virtual time when active.

Address-space cache state allocates a group, snapshots per-CPU runtime and epoch values, initializes lock, epoch, unassigned CPU marker, next scan time and zeroed averages, sets reference count to one, then publishes per-CPU pointer and group pointer with release ordering so reachable groups are fully initialized. References are acquired only from non-zero counts, released through RCU-deferred freeing, and transferred across fork, failed fork cleanup, exec remapping, thread exit with footprint convergence, and address-space teardown.

Group lock serializes epoch advancement and deferred-work queuing. CPU epoch lock with interrupt saving guards runtime refresh during occupancy sampling. RCU guards pointer publication and lookup, with plain initialization only before visibility and compare-only access where dereference is not needed.

Occupancy fraction scales sampled runtime against CPU runtime under lock after refresh. Tick path is inert when caching is disabled, group or per-CPU state is missing, target is a kernel thread, or epoch has not advanced; otherwise under group lock it queues single-shot deferred work once and records the epoch. Deferred work enforces rate limiting with single-scanner election, skips invalid or over-capacity placements while clearing preference, builds a scan mask honoring preferred and current NUMA locality or all online CPUs, accumulates per-LLC occupancy to select the busiest LLC, applies twofold hysteresis before moving preference, and smooths observed runnable count with an LLC-size-scaled divisor clamped between two and eight.
Scheduler invokes fair current update that refreshes each enclosing queue along the donor entity chain, and invokes a per-task cache tick hook that may be compiled to no operation.

Wait, sleeper and enqueue accounting run only when scheduler statistics are enabled, resolving counters from the entity and distinguishing task from group ownership; enqueue of a non-current head starts wait accounting and wakeup enqueues add sleeper accounting; execution start stamps the entity with the queue task clock.
